chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda al-Hazza, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a boy and a girl who were married by their guardians, and both of them were not yet mature. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The marriage is valid, and whichever of the two matures, he/she will have the choice (to annul or confirm). And if they die before they mature, there is no inheritance between them, nor any dower, except if both had matured and were pleased (with the marriage).'

I said, 'What if one of them matures before the other?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is allowed upon him if he is pleased.' I said, 'What if the man who matured before the girl, and was pleased with the marriage, then died before the girl matured? Would she inherit him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, her inheritance from him is set aside until she matures. Then she swears by Allah that what prompted her to take the inheritance is only her consent to the marriage. Then the inheritance is handed over to her, and half the dower.'

I said, 'What if the girl died and she had not yet matured? Would the mature husband inherit her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because she has the choice when she matures.' I said, 'What if her father was the one who married her before she matured?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The father's marriage is valid upon her, and it is valid upon the boy, and the dower is upon the father for the girl.'

key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: The option/choice (to annul or confirm marriage upon maturity)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status and consequences of a marriage contracted for children who have not yet reached puberty?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of *nikah al-sighar* (child marriage), establishing that while a guardian's contract is valid, it remains contingent upon the child's option of maturity (*khiyar al-balagh*) upon reaching puberty. The text provides detailed procedural rulings for inheritance and dower (*mahr*) distribution, particularly highlighting the mechanism of withholding assets until the surviving party swears an oath of consent if they die before the other reaches maturity. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the balance between guardian authority and the individual's right to confirm or reject the union upon attaining legal capacity.
